page: The UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-2xL4 is a GPU-family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 CPU architecture with 20 shared vCPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.8 GB per vCPU. Acceleration is provided by two NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 48 GB of VRAM.

This server configuration does not include local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met through external block storage volumes. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. A key architectural tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which may introduce resource contention under sustained, non-GPU-bound CPU workloads compared to dedicated thread allocations.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high memory density and dual-GPU acceleration on a shared-CPU hypervisor framework, making it a specialized option for workloads that require significant GPU memory and system RAM without needing dedicated, high-frequency physical CPU cores. This hardware profile is designed for workloads such as machine learning inference, data science jobs, and GPU-accelerated rendering or analytical tasks.
